_about: THE ONE CONFIG for the for sale SYNC's spending (Lane D, Nov 19 2026). A person changes numbers here and nothing else decides them. Every number is vendor queries (one a page of 100 listings). THE SYNC: each source is loaded once (resumable, and it serves nothing until its load is finished: the 14 dealers are 42 queries), then every run polls that source for CHANGES (changed_since with the saved checkpoint) and for STALE listings (last_seen_before 24 hours ago, hidden not deleted): at least 2 queries a source a run, 28 for the 14 dealers, more when over 100 listings changed in a window. SET FOR THE 14 DEALERS PLUS classiccars, dupontregistry and barnfinds (17 sources, twice a day), autotraderclassics OFF, and THE SCHEDULE IS ON on Sam's word (Nov 19 2026): both schedule flags are true and vercel.json carries the two cron lines. TO SWITCH OFF it takes only ONE of them (set the flags false here, or delete the two lines); the way it was switched on took BOTH: set schedule.pull_on and schedule.prepare_on to true here AND add two lines to the crons in vercel.json: path /api/pullForSale?mode=pull with schedule 10 */12 * * * (00:10 and 12:10 UTC), and path /api/pullForSale?mode=prepare with schedule 40 * * * *. Either alone fires nothing (a call that arrives as the platform's scheduled one is refused while its flag is false, and a flag with no cron line is never called). For the 14 dealers alone, twice a day costs 56 queries a day (1,680 a month) when few listings change and at most 80 a day (2,400 a month) when every listing changes once a day, plus 42 once for the load (Lane F's counts, 3,498 listings), plus one to read the vendor's remaining count when no fresh reading is kept: THE 17 SOURCES: the load is 427 queries (460 with margin) and a poll run is 34 queries when nothing changed (68 a day twice a day, 104 a day when 10 percent of listings change); work order is change polls, then stale polls, then loads, so a load takes what the polls leave and resumes at its saved page. forsale_run_cap 120 lets a load run go on for 120 pages (about four runs for the whole load) and forsale_monthly_budget 2800 sits inside the room (plan_monthly minus auction_reserve_monthly = 3,000): the 17 sources at twice a day fit only if under about 9 percent of listings change a day, and a run that would pass the budget or the reserve stops and says so. A larger set loads over several runs (a run stops at its cap and resumes at the saved page): B (dealers plus classiccars, dupontregistry, barnfinds) is a 427 query load, (forsale_run_cap is already 120 for it). sync.lapse_hours 30: a source whose change poll or stale poll has not finished within that time is not served at all: at twice a day one missed run is tolerated and two in a row take the source dark, rather than leave dead cars up. A budget or a run cap of 0 pulls nothing. The for sale sync can never spend the auction feed's allowance: auction_reserve_monthly is a hard reserve (the sync's room is at most plan_monthly minus it, and a run also needs the vendor's own remaining count to stay above the reserve for the days left in the cycle). A run that would pass any limit stops at once and the report says which limit and where; no run ever marks a listing gone because a walk ended. A source can be switched by its own name under pull (a boolean under a source's name wins over its group).
auction_use_basis: The auction feed's use this cycle, DERIVED from figures Lane F posted (plan 10,000; 4,963 remained before its pull; its pull took 1,035; the cycle resets about the 25th): 10,000 - 4,963 = 5,037 used in the 24 days since Oct 25, which is about 210 a day, about 6,300 a month. 7,000 is that plus about 10 percent. Not read from the usage table: correct it from app_usage_events (the report route prints the measured figure). The vendor's own header on Nov 18 read limit 10000, remaining 4124, reset Nov 25 04:27 UTC.
